title: SeaFlux: harmonization of air–sea CO2 fluxes from surface pCO2 data products using a standardized approach
testbed_rationale: This paper harmonizes air-sea CO2 flux calculations from existing mapped observation-based products rather than developing or testing an ML parameterization suitable for a climate model.
pain_points: Differences in spatial coverage across mapped pCO2 products (omission of coastal, Arctic, and marginal seas) required artificial filling with climatology
Inconsistent scaling of wind-speed dependent gas transfer velocity coefficient (kw) between products and reanalyses

Order of operations sensitivity: calculating the second moment of wind speed at high temporal/spatial native resolution vs time-averaged wind speeds severely affects flux due to nonlinearity (concavity)
extraction_notes: The study itself does not train a new ML parameterization, but harmonizes fluxes from existing ML and statistical mapping products (CMEMS-FFNN, CSIR-ML6, MPI-SOMFFN, NIES-FNN, JMA-MLR) and mixed-layer scheme (JENA-MLS).
